sections.h2: How can I sell a house in Lancaster, NY?
sections.html:
You can hire a listing agent, sell on your own, or take an as-is cash offer, and the choice mostly turns on timing and the condition of the house. A Lancaster owner with a newer home in good shape and no deadline has the most room to list. An owner facing a probate, a tenant problem or a stack of repairs often cares more about a firm closing date than the last few thousand dollars.

  • List with an agent: you get market exposure, but you also take on showings, buyer financing and appraisal risk.
  • Sell by owner: you keep control of price and terms, and you handle the contract, disclosures and paperwork with your attorney.
  • Cash offer: the buyer purchases the house in its current state, so repairs and cleanouts are off your list.

Whichever route you pick, the same Lancaster steps follow: a deed signed before a notary, transfer tax forms filed with the Erie County Clerk, and a payoff of any property tax still owed.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Lancaster itself?
sections.html:
Lancaster is a town in Erie County, about 11 miles east of downtown Buffalo, with roughly 37 square miles of land and two villages inside it: Lancaster and Depew. The town's own history page says it became a separate town in 1833, split from Clarence, and that the Village of Lancaster was incorporated in 1849 and Depew in 1894. Five major railroads once crossed the town, and rail lines still run through it.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 45,075 residents, almost unchanged from the 45,106 counted in 2020. Most of the town sits in the Lancaster Central School District, but the Town tax office also lists Depew Union Free, Alden Central, Clarence Central and Iroquois Central as districts that bill Lancaster addresses. Check the district on your tax bill before you tell a buyer which schools apply.

Road access is a selling point for commuters. The Thruway (I-90) crosses the northern part of town, NY 33 runs just south of it, and US 20 (Broadway) cuts through the middle. NY 78, known as Transit Road, marks the western edge. The eastern side, beyond Bowen Road, is newer and more open, while the older housing stock sits closer to the village centers.

sections.h2: What do Lancaster housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
Lancaster is a town of owners with a median home value of $277,600, far below the Long Island prices elsewhere in New York. The table below lists the Census figures most sellers ask about. Pair them with recent sales your agent or buyer can show you, because a five-year survey median does not price a single house.

sections.h2: Which Lancaster permits and inspections can affect a sale?
sections.html:
The Lancaster Building Department can affect a sale if past work on the house was done without a permit, since it enforces the state building code, zoning and flood plain rules for both the town and the village. Its department page states that anyone who builds, alters, moves or demolishes a building or structure must first obtain a permit.

The department posts separate applications for decks, fences, pools and hot tubs, sheds and demolition, plus a handout on as-built survey requirements. If a deck, finished basement or addition went in before you bought, ask the office whether the work is on file and closed out. A buyer's attorney will usually ask the same question, and a clear answer shortens negotiations.

  • Pools, decks and sheds each have their own application form.
  • The department lists a page for vacant and "zombie" properties, useful if you inherited a house that has sat empty.
  • Inspections on a permit are scheduled by calling the office, which is open Monday through Friday during business hours.

The town also posts a map of approved truck routes and a yard sale permit, which are handled at the Highway Department on Pavement Road.

sections.h2: When are Lancaster property taxes due, and what if they are unpaid?
sections.html:
Town and County taxes are due February 15 and school taxes are due October 15, moving to the next business day when a date lands on a weekend or holiday. The Lancaster tax office, which sits within the Town Clerk's office, collects both. Mail counts as on time only with a postmark on or before the due date, and the page says there are no exceptions.

Late school tax carries a 7.5% penalty for the rest of October and 9% in November. Anything still unpaid after November 30 moves to the Erie County tax roll, and that deadline is two weeks out as of today's date. For Town and County tax, penalties climb from 1.5% in the first two weeks after the due date up to 7.5% by the end of April, with interest added on top after that.

The Town tax office takes Town and County payments through June 30 and school payments through November 30. After those dates, payments and payoff requests go to Erie County Real Property Tax Services in Buffalo. If you plan to sell a house with delinquent tax, get a county payoff figure before choosing a closing date, since interest changes the amount month to month.

sections.h2: What does transferring a Lancaster house cost at the county clerk?
sections.html:
The seller pays the transfer tax at the Erie County Clerk, at a combined $4.50 for each $500 of the sale price, with $2.00 going to New York State and $2.50 to the county. The Clerk's deed page says the price is rounded up to the next $500. On a house that sold at the town's $277,600 median value, that works out to about $2,502 before any recording charges.

Recording itself costs a $45 statutory fee plus $5 per page, a $10 fee to file the TP-584 transfer tax form, and $125 to file the RP-5217 transfer report for residential property. The deed must be original, signed and notarized, with the full legal description and street addresses for every party, because P.O. boxes are not accepted.

  • Owners aged 62 or older who have lived in a one- or two-family home for at least a year can claim a reduced rate of $2.00 per $500.
  • A 1% mansion tax applies to residential sales of $1 million or more, and the state says the buyer pays it.
  • For residential property, the Clerk also asks for a Notice of Sale or Transfer of Ownership form.

Under state rules summarized on the Tax Department's transfer tax page, the TP-584 and payment are due within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

sections.h2: Should I close my Lancaster STAR registration when I sell?
sections.html: Yes. The state tells owners who sell a property to close their STAR registration, and the new owner registers for their own credit once the house is their primary residence. If your school tax is paid through a mortgage escrow account, your lender is the one to ask about any escrow refund after closing.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on a Lancaster house?
faqs.a: The Lancaster tax office, part of the Town Clerk's office, collects Town, County and school tax for the school districts inside the town. After June 30 for Town and County bills and after November 30 for school bills, payments go to Erie County Real Property Tax Services instead.

faqs.q: Which school districts serve Lancaster homes?
faqs.a: Lancaster Central, Depew Union Free, Alden Central, Clarence Central and Iroquois Central all bill taxes on Lancaster properties, according to the town tax office. Most of the town falls in Lancaster Central, so confirm the district on your own bill.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax when a Lancaster house sells?
faqs.a: The seller pays the New York State and Erie County transfer tax when the deed is presented to the County Clerk. The combined rate is $4.50 per $500 of the price, and a reduced $2.00 rate may apply to qualifying owners aged 62 or older.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit just to sell my Lancaster house?
faqs.a: No permit is listed for a plain sale. The Building Department's permit rule covers building, altering, moving and demolishing structures, so ask the office whether any earlier deck, addition or pool work on your house was permitted and finished.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lancaster house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can list it as is, sell it to an investor or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases without repair requests. Expect the price to reflect the condition, and ask the Building Department about any open permit before you accept an offer.
